author: Ethan Goode
title: Port Allen leaders consider land purchase for wastewater treatment facility - NewsBreak
text:
By Ethan Goode ,
5 hours ago
PORT ALLEN, La. (Louisiana First) — As Port Allen continues to grow, city leaders are taking steps they say could help prepare the city for future development.
During Wednesday’s committee meeting, officials discussed acquiring approximately 31 acres of land for a proposed municipal wastewater treatment facility. The proposal includes obtaining an independent appraisal of the property and authorizing a contingent purchase agreement pending environmental reviews and site suitability studies.
City leaders say the project is aimed at ensuring the city’s infrastructure can support future growth while addressing long-term wastewater and drainage needs.
Officials noted that the proposed site could provide additional land and improve drainage opportunities in the area.
“We still have to be good citizens of the taxpayers’ dollars,” Port Allen Mayor Terecita Pollard Patton said during the discussion.
Before any final decision is made, the city plans to complete several evaluations, including environmental assessments and an independent appraisal to determine the property’s value and suitability for the project.
Leaders say those steps are intended to protect taxpayers while ensuring the city is making a sound investment for the future.
The discussion also included plans for a future budget amendment that would allocate funds for the land purchase if the project moves forward.
Officials emphasized that the wastewater treatment facility remains in the planning stages, but they say investing in infrastructure now could help position Port Allen for continued residential and commercial growth in the years ahead.
The proposal will continue to be reviewed as city leaders gather additional information about the property, project costs, and potential benefits to the community.
